title: en or et: learn the word with its article
objective: Use en and et with everyday nouns and recognise that most nouns take en.
explanation: Every Danish noun is either an en-word or an et-word: “en kop” (a cup), “et glas” (a glass). About three in four nouns take en, but there is no reliable rule for the rest, so learn each noun together with its article, as one unit: not “kop” but “en kop”. Your phrase cards show an en-word or et-word badge to help.
sourceReference: Deepwater original starter course (2026-10-29), written for Echo; teacher review required before publishing.

exercises.feedbackCorrect: Right: “en kop kaffe”. Kop is an en-word.
exercises.feedbackIncorrect: Kop is an en-word: “en kop kaffe”.

exercises.feedbackCorrect: Right: “et hus”. Hus is an et-word.
exercises.feedbackIncorrect: Hus is one of the et-words: “et hus”.

exercises.prompt: Write three things you can see right now, each with en or et. Look up any article you are not sure of, and save the words as cards.
